items.title: Theorem 6.6: real-rooted weighted determinant mixtures of paired rank-one updates
items.statement_scope: Let $a_1,\dotsc,a_m$ and $b_1,\dotsc,b_m$ be vectors in $\mathbb R^n$, let $p_1,\dotsc,p_m$ be real numbers in $[0,1]$, and let $D$ be a positive semidefinite matrix. Then every univariate polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[m]}(\prod_{i\in S}p_i)(\prod_{i\notin S}(1-p_i))\det(xI+D+\sum_{i\in S}a_i a_i^T+\sum_{i\notin S}b_i b_i^T)$ is real-rooted.

items.difficulty_reason: author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H3. The proof constructs the multivariate determinant $Q=\det(xI+D+\sum_i u_i a_i a_i^T+\sum_i v_i b_i b_i^T)$ (IF1.tex:885-889), proves the subset-sum identity by induction using zero substitutions and $T_i=1+p_i\partial_{u_i}+(1-p_i)\partial_{v_i}$ (891-922), and applies real-stability preservation and real-variable restrictions to conclude $P$ is real-rooted (924-925). This is a substantial research-bearing argument, not a routine corollary.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Constructs a real-stable multivariate determinant, proves the subset-sum identity by induction with $T_i=1+p_i\partial_{u_i}+(1-p_i)\partial_{v_i}$ and zero substitutions, and applies stability closure to obtain real-rootedness.

semantic_comparisons.basis: Quasi-perfect Lee codes and abelian Ramanujan graph counting; no real-rootedness or expected determinant polynomial statement.
Coefficient relation for Narayana polynomials; different polynomial family, hypotheses and conclusion.
Zero interlacing and Wronskian-type bounds for orthogonal polynomials; a different interlacing setting, not real stability of expected determinants from rank-one updates.
Local h-polynomials and uniform triangulations; real-rootedness application but a different combinatorial theorem and proof.
Splitting of Breuil-Kisin modules and Ext vanishing; unrelated algebraic-module objects and conclusion.
Real-rootedness of Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials for thagomizer and K_{2,n} graphic matroids; different polynomials and a different pencil argument.
Homology of spaces of real polynomials with prescribed root multiplicities; homology computation, not real stability or expected determinant real-rootedness.
Tau-polynomial real-rootedness under graph joins and a coefficient-substitution lemma; different graph polynomial and different conclusion.

Determinantal representations of a quadrature-node curve; determinant representation is an analogous device, but the result concerns Gaussian quadrature nodes, not real-rootedness of every expected characteristic polynomial with arbitrary rank-one updates.

Finite free Stam inequality for monic real-rooted polynomials; real-rootedness is present, but the statement is an inequality under finite free convolution, not a real-stability/expected-determinant theorem.
